content.title: St. Patrick’s Day in Chicago 2026 | Parades & River Dyeing
content.text: There’s nothing quite like St. Patrick’s Day in Chicago, when Irish taverns fill with revelers, cultural celebrations pop up in every corner of the city, and the Chicago River sparkles brilliant shades of emerald green.St. Patrick's Day events in ChicagoThe history of St. Patrick’s Day in Chicago goes back more than 175 years. Now a longstanding tradition, Chicago’s Irish parade was first held in 1843. The dyeing of the Chicago River was added in 1962, quickly becoming one of Chicago’s most famous events.St. Patrick’s Day in Chicago HighlightsTop events of Chicago’s iconic St. Patrick’s Day celebrations include:The annual green river dyeing, when the Chicago River turns bright green for the dayThe downtown St. Patrick’s Day parade, a beloved multi-generational traditionPub crawls and dining specials in every corner of the city, including famous Irish pubs like Chief O’Neill’s and Cork & KerryA variety of neighborhood parades and events, like the local-favorite South Side Irish ParadeAlong with the downtown festivities, Chicago’s proud Irish heritage is also on full display in our neighborhoods — from Beverly (a traditionally Irish enclave) to the Irish American Heritage Center near Albany Park.Explore the top ways to celebrate St. Patrick’s Day with events and things to do in Chicago.Chicago River Dyeing​​Saturday, March 14, 2026The annual Chicago River dyeing is one of the most unique St. Patrick’s Day celebrations in the world. Typically held the Saturday before St. Patrick’s Day (the same day as the downtown parade), this bucket-list event is a beloved tradition that dates back over half a century. The best place to watch the green river dyeing is along the Chicago River between State and Columbus. Spectators can watch from Upper Wacker and the many bridges; the lower Riverwalk will be closed except for select ticketed events.The green river dyeing starts at 10 a.m. Get there early for a good view and to watch the eco-friendly dye flowing from various boats. The brilliant green color only lasts a few hours, so be sure to catch a glimpse and snap some photos before heading off to a local tavern to enjoy some green beer.Explore more: Discover where to watch the Chicago River dyeing with our guide to waterfront bars and restaurants.Chicago St. Patrick’s Day Parade​​​​Saturday, March 14, 2026 Theannual Chicago St. Patrick’s Day Parade is one of the largest in the country and the centerpiece of the city’s unforgettable St. Patrick’s Day celebrations. Catch the festive procession on Columbus Drive between Balbo Drive and Monroe Drive.Don your best green outfit or kilt and grab a good spot before the parade begins at noon. You won’t want to miss The Shannon Rovers Irish Pipe Band, the city’s premier Irish band, who have been leading the procession since the first official parade in 1956. You’ll alsosee plenty of colorful floats waving their Irish flags high, troops of Irish step dancers, marching bands, bagpipers, and more during the three-hour celebration. St. Patrick’s Day river cruises​​Saturday, March 14, 2026 Admire the emerald green river from the best seats in the house. City Cruises invites guests aboard the Chicago St. Patrick’s Day River Dyeing Cruise, offering unparalleled views of one of Chicago’s most beloved traditions. The 10:00 AM departure provides exclusive dockside access during the dyeing process, giving guests the best possible vantage point to watch the river turn emerald green. Guests will enjoy festive Irish music, skyline views, and a lively atmosphere throughout the cruise. And for those looking to elevate the celebration, guests are welcome to bring their own snacks and their favorite Irish beer to enjoy onboard, perfect for toasting to Chicago’s biggest day in style.St. Patrick’s Day Clover Cruise from Chicago’s First LadySt. Patrick’s Day Cruise from Wendella CruisesArchitecture River Cruise from Shoreline SightseeingSt. Patrick’s Day Premier Lunch Cruise from City CruisesDiscover all of Chicago’s river cruises.South Side Irish ParadeSunday, March 15, 2026A long-time tradition, the 48th annual South Side Irish Parade is a homegrown, family-friendly celebration of Irish heritage. Join the thousands of fellow revelers who gather to watch the bands, dance troupes, and this year’s newly crowned parade queen. The parade takes place the day after the downtown celebrations and marches south on Western Avenue between 103rd and 115th Streets. After the parade, take some time to explore Chicago’s Beverly neighborhood, one of the city’s longest-standing Irish communities. Stop inside one of the area’s many neighborhood bars to raise a pint with the locals.Festivals and partiesLooking for some corned beef and cabbage? How about the perfect pint of Guinness? Maybe you’re searching for a spot to grab a bite while watching the Chicago River dyeing? Well, you’re in the right place! Celebrate St. Patrick’s Day at one of the many riverfront restaurants and bars in the city that offer a prime view of the green river dyeing. And check out the many street festivals, parties, and bars and restaurants going all out for the holiday.Check out our round-up of festive St. Patrick’s Day restaurant and bar specials all around Chicago.More St. Patrick’s Day neighborhood eventsNorthwest Side Irish ParadeCome enjoy this fun community event that has been celebrating friends, family, and Irish heritage for more than 20 years. The Northwest Side Irish Parade kicks off at noon on Sunday, March 15, 2026 and winds through the Norwood Park neighborhood, beginning at William J. Onahan School. St. Patrick’s Day events at the Irish American Heritage CenterHead to the northwest side to visit the Irish American Heritage Center, which will be hosting an array of events leading up to St. Patrick’s Day, including an Irish singing workshop and concert, a Celtic art class, and more.Shamrock’n at Old St. Patrick’s Church This West Loop church is hosting its annual pop-up Irish pub, Shamrock’n the Block, on Saturday, March 14, 2026. Enjoy live entertainment, food, a raffle, and a heated tent beer garden. This all-ages event will also feature activities for kids.
